label: D1 after a common a2->S2 trial (agent about to repeat a2)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO or D2). Within the window, (D1 & prev_action==2 & prev_common==1), meaning the previous trial chose a2 and reached S2 by a common transition, has precision 1.00 but recall 0.69, because on the window first trial (rel -3) the previous trial falls outside the window and prev_action is unknown. For those steps I use the agent upcoming choice (action==2 at D1) as a stand-in. That is a choice the agent computes itself, not a random outcome, and it is strongly correlated because the agent usually stays after a2->S2c. This gives dev F1 0.90 and mass recall 0.97. The purely observed alternative (D1 & prev_state==2) scores F1 0.82, and action==2 alone at D1 scores F1 0.78. The feature does NOT fire after rare transitions (a2->S1 or a1->S2) or after a1->S1 trials, apart from weak low-quartile activations. Magnitude: in the examples, after an unrewarded a2->S2c trial (r0) the activation is near max (~0.97-1.0), and after a rewarded one (r1) it is ~0.83-0.87. Among active steps, policy logits leaning moderately toward a2 at D1 are enriched.

issues: I reproduced the reported scores. Test split: P 0.939, R 0.871, F1 0.904, mass recall 0.966. Dev: F1 0.905.
'Fires only at D1' holds: GO and D2 have 0 active steps out of 380,619 each.

The core clause checks out. On D1 steps with rel > -3, prev_action==2 & prev_common==1 has precision 1.000 on dev. Split by prev_reward, both halves keep precision 1.000 (rewarded R 0.50, unrewarded R 0.19). Unrewarded is enriched in the top activation quartile (0.50 vs 0.31 coverage), which matches the magnitude claim.

On test, every false positive I sampled is at rel -3, where the action==2 stand-in is used (rel -3 & action==2: precision 0.77). This is a limit of the window, not a gap in the explanation. An observed-only stand-in, (rel==-3) & (choice<0) using the D1 policy logit, does as well: test F1 0.901 vs 0.904. The record could have used it and avoided uses_future.

The parenthetical 'agent about to repeat a2' slightly overclaims. After a2->S2 common, the feature fires with precision 1.000 even when the agent then switches to a1 (n=6,347, though the activation is weaker: 0.13 of the lowest quartile, ~0 of the top). It reflects the previous trial, not the upcoming choice.

There is one systematic weak class the explanation only hedges ('apart from weak lowest-quartile activations'): D1 after a rare a1->S2 transition. Precision there is 0.42 overall and 0.49 when unrewarded. These activations are all in the lowest quartile (~31-38% of lowest-quartile actives) and hold about 2% of activation mass. Some are not that weak: one example after an unrewarded a1->S2 rare trial, where the agent switched to a2, reached 0.62. Read loosely, the feature is 'D1 after reaching S2', strongest after a common a2 transition. Adding this clause raises test F1 only to 0.912 (precision drops to 0.878), so the original predicate is still reasonable.
D1 after a common a1->S1 trial: precision 0.000. D1 after a rare a2->S1 trial: precision 0.026. Both are consistent with the claims.
